sources: dossier=Superseded/historical: 'on_event validation against Capabilities.declared_events... appears on the 2026-07-11 transcript retired-mechanisms list... doc or code presenting declared-events as current is drift'; doc=What-it-is said entry shape 'includes the service's declared events'; code=ObservabilityCapabilities (discovery.go:40-57) carries DeclaredTags, DeclaredErrorClasses, ExpectedAttributesSchema, no events field.

sources: dossier=Superseded/historical (declared-events retirement, transcript tier) plus Required behaviors bullet noting 'the declared-events portion is affected by a later transcript retirement'; doc=Purpose named a 'subscription declared-events cross-check' and an 'unknown event names treated as no-ops' runtime rule; code=template_validator.go implements a payload-tags check, an error-class vocabulary check, and instances_static_config_gate.go/instances.go implement an expected-attributes schema gate; expected_attributes_schema_resolver.go resolves the schema at dispatch; no no-op fallback exists anywhere in lib/graph or lib/runtime.
note: The two named consumers are fabricated per the dossier's transcript-tier declared-events retirement, and no unreachable-at-registration no-op fallback exists in the design corpus or code. Rewrote Purpose to name the real registration-time (tag cross-check, error-class vocabulary check, expected-attributes schema gate) and dispatch-time (expected-attributes schema resolution) consumers.

sources: dossier=silent on internal index shape; design corpus=observability.md:11 establishes 'two optional gRPC protocols total, one per service kind' (executor-observability vs claim-producer-observability), corroborating a kind split; code=discovery.go:72-77 holds separate executors/stores maps with kind-scoped GetExecutor/GetStore, ListExecutors/ListClaimProducers; doc=said only 'Indexed by service name'.
note: No dossier entry disputes this; observability.md's kind-split protocol framing corroborates (without literally stating) that the cache mirrors it, and the code is unambiguous and uncontested. Rewrote 'Indexed by service name' to describe the two kind-partitioned indexes, each keyed by name within its kind.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'Claim producers may declare declared_error_classes in their capabilities response, stored in the cache at handshake; declaring nothing remains legal' (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability, artifact-only); code=bundled.go:48-61 executor loop sets Schema+Tags+ErrorClasses, :62-70 claim-producer loop sets only DeclaredErrorClasses; doc=said the bundled path populates 'each in-proc handler's schema, tags, and declared error classes' with no kind distinction.
note: The dossier explicitly scopes claim-producer capabilities to declared_error_classes only, directly corroborating the code and refuting the doc's undifferentiated claim. Rewrote the What-it-is paragraph to distinguish the executor advertisement (schema, tags, error classes) from the claim-producer advertisement (error classes only).
